text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian oil workers demanding higher pay release 28 foreigners held on a vessel offshore near southeastern Eket town
- Discussions begin between Oil Ministry officials and the Federal Environmental Protection Agency (FEPA) on reducing pollution through the removal of lead from petroleum products.
- Nigeria plans to introduce trading in derivatives to boost investment opportunities in the capital market.
- Twenty robbers in northern Borno attack and steal 100,000 naira cash and valuables from 30 members of one of five registered political parties returning from a campaign.
- Improved medical and welfare services in Nigeria's 147 prisons have brought a considerable reduction in death rate among inmates, Comptroller-General Ibrahim Jama says.
- State-run power company National Electric Power Authority to jettison rural electrification programme when it begins full commercial operations next year.
- Experts say Nigeria loses $160 million annually and the leather industry may collapse due to the high rate consumption of the non-nutritional cow skin.
